title.en: The future seen from the past
title.es: El futuro visto desde el pasado

summary.en: When we tell a story or report plans, we often look forward from a moment in the past. Use **was/were going to** for a plan or intention (often one that did not happen): _I was going to call you, but I forgot._ Use **was/were about to** for something that was just going to happen: _We were about to leave when it started to rain._ Use **would** to describe what turned out to be the future, with hindsight: _She didn't know she would become a minister._ In formal or literary style, **was/were to** and **was/were to have + past participle** describe events that were arranged, fated, or planned but did not happen: _The talks were to have begun on Monday._ These forms are useful for narratives and for formal reports of missed plans in Writing part 4.
summary.es: Es el «iba a…», «estaba a punto de…» y «llegaría a ser…» del español. Ojo: would no sirve para un plan que no se cumplió; para eso usa was going to o was to have + participio.

form: Plan or intention: **was/were going to + infinitive**
Unfulfilled plan: **was/were going to + infinitive** (often with _but_) or **was/were to have + past participle** (formal)
Hindsight about what happened next: **would + infinitive** (_He would later regret it._)
Arrangements or fate: **was/were to + infinitive** (_She was to become a famous novelist._)
Past continuous for arrangements: _I was meeting Ana at six._
Negative: _I wasn't going to say anything._ / _It would never be the same again._

uses.text: **Plans that did not happen** → _We were going to book a table, but the restaurant was full._
**Just about to happen** → _Just as the plane was about to take off, a passenger asked to get off._
**Hindsight in narrative** → _Nobody then realised that this small start-up would become a global brand._

note.en: Would here looks forward from the past, so it does not change into will.
note.es: Mira hacia delante desde el pasado: no se convierte en will.

uses.text: **Fate or destiny (formal, literary)** → _They were to meet again twenty years later._
**Formal report of a cancelled plan** → _The ceremony was to have taken place in June; it has been postponed._

mistakes.wrong: I would call you last night, but I forgot.
mistakes.right: I was going to call you last night, but I forgot.

why.en: Would does not express an unfulfilled plan; use was going to (or was to have called in formal style).
why.es: Para un plan que no se cumplió: was going to, no would.

mistakes.wrong: She was about leaving when the phone rang.
mistakes.right: She was about to leave when the phone rang.

why.en: Be about is followed by to + infinitive, not an -ing form.

mistakes.wrong: He didn't know that he will win the prize.
mistakes.right: He didn't know that he would win the prize.

why.en: After a past tense, the future from that moment is would, not will.
why.es: Tras un verbo en pasado, usa would, no will.

examples.en: I was going to book a table, but the restaurant was already full.
examples.es: Iba a reservar mesa, pero el restaurante ya estaba lleno.

examples.en: We were about to leave when the manager called.
She didn't know it yet, but she would soon be running the whole department.
He left home at eighteen, never imagining that he would one day return as mayor.
examples.es: Se fue de casa a los dieciocho, sin imaginar que un día volvería como alcalde.

examples.en: The talks were to have started on Monday, but both delegations arrived late.
They were to meet again twenty years later, in a very different city.
I was meeting Ana at six, so I couldn't stay for the film.
Nobody told us the road was going to be closed.
It was the last time he would ever see the village.
Just as the train was about to leave, a man ran along the platform.
I wasn't going to mention the mistake, but she asked me directly.
examples.es: No pensaba mencionar el error, pero me preguntó directamente.

practice.prompt: I ___ ring you last night, but my phone ran out of battery.

explanation.en: A plan that did not happen: was going to + infinitive.

practice.prompt: I was about ___ the door when the phone rang.

explanation.en: Be about is followed by to + infinitive.

practice.prompt: Nobody realised then that the little start-up ___ one of the biggest firms in Europe.

explanation.en: Looking forward from a past moment, with hindsight: would + infinitive.

practice.prompt: The new bridge ___ opened in May, but heavy rain has delayed the work.

explanation.en: Was/were to have + past participle: a formal way to say a plan did not happen.
